lines.text: Does the Control Center Wi-Fi button really turn Wi-Fi off?
Most people tap it and assume it is off. Apple's support page says it only disconnects.
The radio stays on, so AirDrop, AirPlay, your Apple Watch and Location Services keep working.
Wi-Fi auto join stays paused until you turn it back on, reach a new place, hit five in the morning, or restart.
To switch it fully off, open Settings, tap Wi-Fi, and turn it off. Bluetooth works the same way.
Here's the catch: Apple itself says to keep Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on for the best experience.

post.title: Does the Control Center Wi-Fi button turn Wi-Fi off?
post.caption:
Does the Control Center Wi-Fi button really turn Wi-Fi off? 📶 Not completely: it disconnects.

Apple's support page says that when you tap the Wi-Fi or Bluetooth button in Control Center, your iPhone immediately disconnects, but both radios stay available, so AirDrop, AirPlay, Apple Pencil, Apple Watch, Handoff, Instant Hotspot, Location Services and Unlock with Apple Watch keep working. Wi-Fi auto-join stays paused until you turn it back on in Control Center, connect to a network in Settings, move to a new location, hit 5 a.m. local time or restart the phone. To switch Wi-Fi or Bluetooth fully off, use Settings > Wi-Fi (or Bluetooth). Apple adds that for the best experience you should try to keep both on.

Send this to a friend who taps that button to save battery.
